newsitem.title: INDIA: Kashmir rebels protest against human rights abuses.
newsitem.headline: Kashmir rebels protest against human rights abuses.

text.p: A strike called to protest against alleged human rights violations by Indian security forces kept shops and schools closed in Kashmir's main city, Srinagar, on Monday.
The two-day strike was called by the All Parties Hurriyat (Freedom) Conference, Kashmir's leading separatist coalition that groups some 30 religious and political organisations.
"We appeal to people of Kashmir to observe a two-day strike from May 12 to protest against gross human rights violations and rape of our women by Indian security forces," a Hurriyat statement said.
Most of the city's streets were deserted and government offices remained closed. Police used tear gas to disperse a rally of demonstrators in Srinagar's Maisuma neighbourhood.

Hurriyat last week said human rights violations by Indian troops, deployed in Kashmir to quell a seven-year-old separatist revolt and to guard India's border with Pakistan, had increased rapidly in recent months. But authorities denied the charges.
"More than 20 women were raped or molested at eight different places during last three months by Indian security forces," a Hurriyat spokesman said.

Authorities have ordered an inquiry into a reported rape case in Srinagar. Three women of Wawoosa village on the city's outskirts were allegedly gang-raped by paramilitary forces, the Hurriyat spokesman said.
Authorities sentenced four Indian soldiers to 10 years imprisonment for raping two women last year in southern Kashmir, an army spokesman said.
On Saturday, police detained a popular separatist leader, Shabir Ahmad Shah, and his supporters for protesting against rights abuses by Indian paramilitary troops.

Dozens of guerrilla groups have been fighting since 1990 for the Himalayan region's merger with neighbouring Pakistan or independence. Police and hospitals say more than 20,000 people have died in insurgency-related violence.
